Client summary
- Age: 26
- Training level: intermediate lifter
- Equipment: full gym access
- Goal: hypertrophy (muscle size)
- Timeframe: 12 weeks

Overview and programming approach
This 12-week program uses progressive overload, planned volume and intensity, exercise variety, and periodized recovery to maximize muscle hypertrophy for an intermediate lifter. It’s structured into three 4-week phases:
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation — build movement quality, baseline volume, and work capacity.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Volume and load emphasis — increase overall weekly volume and introduce heavier sets.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification and peak hypertrophy — highest intensity techniques (short rest, some drop sets/tempo), then a deload week at the end if desired.

Weekly layout (split)
This plan uses a 5-day upper/lower + push/pull/full hybrid to provide frequency and volume per muscle group, suitable for an intermediate lifter:
- Day 1 (Mon): Upper push (chest, shoulders, triceps)
- Day 2 (Tue): Lower heavy (quads, hamstrings, glutes)
- Day 3 (Wed): Upper pull (back, biceps)
- Day 4 (Thu): Rest or active recovery (optional mobility/light cardio)
- Day 5 (Fri): Push (chest, shoulders, triceps) — different emphasis/angles from Day 1
- Day 6 (Sat): Lower volume/hypertrophy or full-body accessory day (glutes, hamstrings, quads, calves, core)
- Day 7 (Sun): Rest

Progression model
- Use weekly progression: small increases in load (2.5–5% where possible) or add 1–2 reps per set when target rep ranges are hit for all sets.
- Every 4th week is a lighter “recovery” week within each 4-week block: Week 4 and Week 8 are reduced volume-intensity weeks (about 60–70% of normal volume/intensity) to consolidate gains and aid recovery. Week 12 is moderate intensity with some light deload options at the end.
- Rest between sets varies with goal: 60–90s for isolation/higher rep work, 90–150s for compound heavier sets. In Phase 3 you’ll shorten some rest to increase metabolic stress.

Warm-up and cooldown
- Begin each session with 8–10 minutes of general warm-up (bike/row/light jog), followed by dynamic mobility for target joints and 2–3 ramp sets for the first compound exercise.
- Finish with 5–10 minutes of mobility/stretching and targeted soft-tissue work as needed.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Calorie target for hypertrophy: ~+250–450 kcal/day above maintenance depending on current body fat and goals. For leaner clients, aim toward the higher end; for those wanting minimal fat gain, target the lower end.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (typical hypertrophy range). If weight not provided, aim for 170–200 g/day for many intermediate males; adjust to client’s mass.
- Carbs: prioritize around training (pre/post) for performance; distribute remaining calories to meet energy target.
- Fats: ~20–30% of calories.
- Hydration, sleep: aim for 7–9 hours sleep/night and consistent hydration.
- Active recovery: include mobility, foam rolling, and low-intensity cardio on rest days when needed.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
General targets: 8–15 working sets per major muscle per week, rep ranges largely 8–15 to build time under tension and muscular endurance. Week 4 is a recovery week (reduce sets ~30–40%).

Week 1

1) Energy (calories)
- Goal: small, controlled calorie surplus to maximize muscle gain while minimizing fat gain.
- Target range: +250 to +400 kcal/day above maintenance.
  - Leaner clients (bodyfat <15%): aim +350 to +400 kcal/day to support faster lean gains.
  - Average/softer clients (bodyfat 15–25%): aim +250 to +300 kcal/day to limit fat gain.
- Practical method: estimate maintenance (TDEE) then add surplus.
  - Quick estimate examples:
    - 70 kg moderately active male: maintenance ~ 2,700–2,900 kcal → target ~ 2,950–3,300 kcal/day.
    - 80 kg moderately active male: maintenance ~ 3,000–3,200 kcal → target ~ 3,250–3,600 kcal/day.
    - 65 kg moderately active female: maintenance ~ 2,000–2,200 kcal → target ~ 2,250–2,600 kcal/day.
- Monitor: weigh client weekly. Expect ~0.25–0.6% bodyweight increase per week (roughly 0.25–0.5 kg/week for many). If weight gain is too fast (>1%/week) reduce calories by 100–200 kcal. If no gain for 2 weeks, increase by 100–200 kcal.

2) Protein
- Target: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (optimal for hypertrophy). For most intermediates, 1.8–2.0 g/kg is practical.
- Example: 80 kg client → 144–176 g protein/day (aim ~160 g).
- Distribution: evenly distribute protein across meals (3–5 protein-containing meals). Aim for 0.4–0.6 g/kg per meal (e.g., 20–40 g per meal) to maximize muscle protein synthesis.

3) Carbohydrates
- Purpose: fuel training, support recovery and glycogen replenishment.
- Target range: 3–6 g/kg bodyweight per day depending on training volume/intensity.
  - Higher-volume weeks (or heavy sessions): aim 4–6 g/kg.
  - Lower-volume/recovery weeks: aim 3–4 g/kg.
- Prioritize higher carb intake around training:
  - Pre-workout: moderate carb + protein 60–90 minutes before (e.g., oats + whey, rice + chicken).
  - Post-workout: 30–90 minutes after: protein + carbs (e.g., rice + lean meat, smoothie with banana + whey).

4) Fats
- Target: ~20–30% of total calories from fat.
- Example: on 3,200 kcal with 25% fat → 800 kcal = ~89 g fat/day.
- Focus on healthy fats: olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocado, oily fish.

5) Meal timing & composition
- Meals per day: 3–6 meals depending on preference. Protein spread evenly is most important.

  - Vitamin D (if low): 1,000–4,000 IU/day depending on levels.

- Main lifts: increase to ~88–92% of pre‑travel working weights. Example:
  - Bench: 4–5 x 4–5 at heavier working sets (RPE 7.5–8.5)
  - Squat: 4–5 x 4–6 heavier
  - Deadlift/Trap bar: 3–4 x 3–5
  - Press: 3–4 x 5–6
- Accessory: maintain or slightly increase accessory volume (10–16 sets/week per large muscle).
- Conditioning: keep conservative intervals; LISS for recovery.
- Recovery: emphasize carbs on heavy days, creatine, sleep.

Week 9 — Bridge (return to pre‑travel Phase 2 loads)
- Main lifts: resume Phase 2 programmed loads (e.g., bench 5 x 5 at pre‑travel working loads if that was the plan).
- Accessory: full Phase 2 accessory volume and exercises.
- Progression: standard rules — add weight 2.5–5% when rep targets are met.

Week 10 — Full Phase 2 continuation
- Continue original Phase 2 progression: heavier sets, increased weekly volume, advanced accessory variations.
- Week 11 will be Phase 3 intensification start.

Phase 3 — Intensification & Peak Hypertrophy (Weeks 11–12)
Goal: highest hypertrophy stimulus, short rest on accessory work, use some intensity techniques. Week 12 is a deload/consolidation.

Week 11 — Intensification
Day 1 — Upper Push
1) Barbell bench press — 5 x 5 (heavier)
2) Incline DB press — 4 x 8–10 (last set drop set optional)
3) Overhead press — 4 x 6–8
4) Lateral raises superset rear delts — 4 x 12/12
5) Cable fly slow eccentrics — 2 x 12–15
6) Close‑grip bench or rope pressdown — 3 x 8–10

Day 2 — Lower Heavy
1) Squat variant (back/front alternate) — 5 x 4–6
2) Romanian deadlift — 4 x 8–10
3) Hip thrust — 4 x 8–12
4) Single‑leg RDL — 3 x 8–10/leg
5) Calf complex — 3 x 12–15 each

Day 3 — Upper Pull
1) Weighted pull‑ups — 5 x 5–6
2) Heavy barbell row — 4 x 6–8
3) Chest‑supported row — 3 x 8–10
4) Face pulls — 4 x 12–15
5) EZ‑bar curls heavy + rest‑pause — 3 x 6–8 + rest‑pause
6) Incline hammer curls — 2 x 12–15

Day 4 — Conditioning A LISS + mobility

Day 5 — Push (intensity techniques)
1) Incline DB press — 4 x 8 with drop set on last
2) Seated DB press — 3 x 8–10 (short rest)
3) Weighted dips — 3 x 6–10
4) Lateral raise cluster sets — 4 clusters
5) Cable crossovers — 3 x 12–15
6) Overhead triceps drop set — 2 x 10 + drop

Day 6 — Lower Hypertrophy / Accessory
1) Deadlift variant (moderate) — 3 x 6–8
2) Leg press — 4 x 10–12 (last set drop-set)
3) Lying leg curl — 4 x 10–12
4) Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10
5) Calves — 4 x 12–15
6) Weighted crunches — 3 x 12–15

Day 7 — Conditioning B (intervals) or Rest

Week 12 — Deload / Consolidation
Option: full deload (recommended)
- Reduce volume and intensity by ~40–50% across the week. Keep movement quality and technique work, but avoid failure and heavy CNS demand.
- Example: perform 2–3 sets per compound exercise at 60–70% usual loads and 2 sets per accessory at moderate intensity. Keep conditioning to light LISS 20 min or rest.

Nutrition plan (lean‑mass gain) — consolidated
1) Calorie target: small controlled surplus +250–400 kcal/day above maintenance. Leaner → higher end; higher body fat → lower end.
- Adjust during travel to maintain surplus; use shakes if appetite reduced.

2) Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (aim 1.8–2.0 g/kg for this client). Spread across 3–5 meals (0.4–0.6 g/kg per meal).

3) Carbohydrates: 3–6 g/kg/day depending on training volume — prioritize pre/post workouts.

4) Fats: ~20–30% total calories from healthy fats.

5) Supplements:
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (continue through travel and reloading).
- Whey protein as needed to hit protein targets.
- Vitamin D and omega‑3s if indicated.

6) Travel nutrition tips:
- Keep protein powder and quick carbs (bananas, rice cakes) handy.
- If low appetite, add caloric smoothies (milk, oats, nut butter, whey).
- Maintain hydration; flights dehydrate.

Conditioning rules with hypertrophy priority
- Two sessions weekly: Thu LISS (20–35 min), Sun intervals (≤3 min total high‑intensity work). Keep conditioning conservative during travel, heavy reintroduction (Week 7), and ramp (Week 8). Replace interval session with LISS or rest if recovery poor.

Progression & monitoring (practical)
- Track weights, sets, reps, and RPE in a training log.
- Small weekly load increases: 2.5–5% where rep targets are met across all sets.
- Weigh weekly mornings; aim for ~0.25–0.6% bodyweight gain per week. Adjust calories ±100–200 kcal as needed.
- Use autoregulation: delay load increases if RPE >8.5 consistently or if rep drops >2 on more than one set.

Return‑to‑heavy checklist (Week 7 practical coaching)
- Warm up thoroughly, ramp sets to working weight each heavy lift.
- Start 5–15% lower than pre‑travel top working weight if unsure.
- Avoid maximal testing in Week 7; use Week 9–10 for heavier testing if desired.
- Reintroduce belt/gear cautiously.

Optional extras I can provide
- Printable day cards for each workout (warm‑ups, ramp sets, tempos, rest times).
- Exact percentage week‑by‑week loads if you send her last pre‑travel working weights for bench, squat, deadlift, and press.
- Condensed 4‑day version if time is limited on travel or return weeks.

If you want the program exported as a printable PDF or CSV for logging, or if you want me to set exact loads based on her last numbers, send those numbers and I’ll generate the updated load‑specific plan.

Below is the complete 12‑week hypertrophy program for your 26‑year‑old intermediate client, updated to include the two‑week travel (hotel‑gym) block in Weeks 5–6 and the reintroduction/reload and deload phases on return. It keeps the original 5‑day split (Upper Push / Lower Heavy / Upper Pull / Push / Lower Hypertrophy) with two conditioning sessions per week (Thu = LISS / mobility, Sun = short intervals or rest). Where the program calls for gym machines or barbells but she’s travelling (Weeks 5–6), the plan switches to dumbbell/unilateral/band alternatives. Week 7 is a conservative reintroduction to heavy barbell work; Weeks 8–10 are a 4‑week ramp back to the Phase 2 trajectory. Week 12 is a planned deload/consolidation week. Nutrition and recovery guidance (lean‑mass focus) is included at the end.

Quick overview
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 Weeks 1–4: Foundation (movement quality, baseline volume)
  - Phase 2 Weeks 5–8: Volume & Load Emphasis — modified: Weeks 5–6 are hotel gym; Week 8 is a lighter recovery week
  - Phase 3 Weeks 9–12: Intensification and peak hypertrophy + deload Week 12 (consolidation)
- Weekly structure:
  - Mon: Upper Push
  - Tue: Lower Heavy
  - Wed: Upper Pull
  - Thu: Conditioning A (LISS) + mobility
  - Fri: Push (variation)
  - Sat: Lower Hypertrophy / Accessory
  - Sun: Conditioning B (intervals) or Rest
- Conditioning: Thu = LISS 20–35 min; Sun = short intervals 12–18 min (or rest if recovery low)
- Progression rules: weekly small load increases (2.5–5%) when rep targets hit; every 4th week lower volume (Weeks 4, 8, 12 as recovery/deload weeks). Use RPE autoregulation.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan

Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
General targets: 8–15 working sets per major muscle per week; compound focus with moderate rep ranges to build work capacity.

Week 1

1) Barbell bench press — 4 x 6–8 (ramp to working sets)
2) Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 8–12
3) Seated overhead press (DB or barbell) — 3 x 8–10

5) Cable chest fly — 2 x 12–15
6) Rope triceps pushdown — 3 x 10–12

Day 2 — Lower Heavy
1) Back squat — 5 x 5–6
2) Romanian deadlift — 3 x 8–10
3) Leg press — 3 x 10–12
4) Walking lunges — 2 x 12 steps/leg
5) Standing calf raise — 4 x 10–15
6) Plank — 3 x 45–60s

Day 3 — Upper Pull
1) Pull-ups (weighted if possible) or lat pulldown — 4 x 6–8
2) Bent-over barbell row — 4 x 6–8
3) Single-arm DB row — 3 x 10–12
4) Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
5) Barbell or DB curls — 3 x 10–12
6) Hammer curls — 2 x 12–15

Day 4 — Conditioning A (LISS 25–30 min) + mobility

Day 5 — Push (variation)
1) Incline dumbbell press — 4 x 8–10
2) Seated Arnold press — 3 x 8–10
3) Weighted dips or machine dips — 3 x 8–10
4) Cable lateral raise (leaning) — 3 x 12–15
5) Pec-deck or incline fly — 2 x 12–15
6) Overhead triceps extension — 3 x 10–12

Day 6 — Lower Hypertrophy / Accessory
1) Front squat or goblet squat — 3 x 8–10
2) Hip thrust — 4 x 8–12
3) Leg curl — 3 x 10–15
4) Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10/leg
5) Seated calf raise — 4 x 10–15

Day 7 — Conditioning B (intervals 12–15 min) or Rest
